item.title: South Korea’s Market Boom—and the Bubble Beneath It
item.description: The South Korean stock market is the world’s best-performing in the first six months of 2026, doubling in value mainly on investors’ perceptions of two companies. But South Korean investors are also at great risk because the euphoric sentiment driving the rally will end someday. This could shock the broader economy, create political fallout, and damage Koreans’ confidence in stock investing.

item.title: Entity List Additions Cool to Their Slowest Pace Since 2008
item.description: Thelack of additions to the Entity Listsince October 2025 marks a sharp break from years of U.S. geoeconomic strategy. Due to the continually shifting nature of procurement networks,a list that stops expanding tracks fewer relevant actors, eroding its value as a control.

item.title: Fortress North America: Mexico’s Role in Securing the Region’s Economic Future
item.description: The 2026 USMCA review is the first test of whether the United States, Mexico, and Canada can turn economic security into a regional framework. Mexico is the hinge, as the top U.S. trading partner, but is also importing from China at a 14-to-1 ratio.

item.description: Democracy is facing its biggest test in decades across Europe. To revive trust in institutions and ensure they deliver what citizens need, leaders must focus on anti-corruption efforts as the key to democratic resilience.

item.description: This CSIS brief offers groundbreaking insight into the value and types of goods flowing through eight different South China Sea chokepoints. The analysis reveals each country’s reliance on each chokepoint and challenges assumptions about their relative importance.

item.title: Reflecting on U.S. Development Policy on the United States’ 250th Anniversary
item.description: As the United States marks its 250th anniversary, it faces a defining question: What role should development play in U.S. global leadership? This commentary explores why development remains central to U.S. strategy, trust, and leadership in an era of disruption.

item.title: What to Know About Chinese AI Models
item.description: Chinese AI models are rapidly closing the gap with U.S. frontier systems. This analysis examines what their growing capabilities, lower costs, and open-weight strategy mean for global AI competition and U.S. policy.

item.title: The United States Has Opted Not to Extend the USMCA
item.description: The United States declined to renew the USMCA for another 16 years, triggering a decade of annual reviews. But the deal did not collapse. It now faces a slower, costlier threat: prolonged uncertainty that stalls investment across North America.
